inputs.text: The “stable” petrol and diesel prices are a public-relations shield, not protection. The excise-duty cuts appear designed to calm people while shifting the bill onto government revenue—and eventually back onto the public through inflation. Calling the situation “precarious” is a way to prepare people for higher costs while pretending no one can know what comes next. That uncertainty is useful to those in power: it lets them control the story and decide when the public is told to accept the consequences.

subtopics: Inflation and costs shifted to the public
